finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id: the boolean result of authorized() is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any project they do not own. The sibling PUT handler uses the throwing authorize() correctly.
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user supplies req.params.id of another user's project

trace.note: project loaded by id with no ownership scoping
authorized() returns a boolean that is ignored; it never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is not used in a condition. There is no throw, abort or return on failure. No router-level middleware is visible in this file. The PUT route at api.js:25 uses authorize(), which throws and so is enforced. A nonexistent id would also make project undefined and cause a TypeError, but that is only a robustness issue.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at api.js:18. The throwing authorize() (api.js:4-10) is used only on the PUT route at api.js:25. No other middleware or ownership scoping exists in the only JS file in the directory.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the bare call `authorized(req.user, project)` discards its boolean result, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated user, owner or not.
